sections.html: Noturus nocturnus Jordan & Gilbert, 1886. Common names: Freckled Madtom, Fregnet Giftmalle (Denmark). Family: Ictaluridae. Size: 15 cm SL. IUCN Red List category: Least Concern (last assessed 2012).
Common name: Freckled madtom. Family: Ictaluridae. Adult size: 12 cm. Temperature: 16–23°C. pH: 6.5–7.2.

North America: Mississippi River basin from northern Illinois to Louisiana, and from eastern Kentucky to central Kansas and Oklahoma in the USA; Gulf Slope drainages from Mobile Bay in Alabama to Guadalupe River in Texas, USA.

Type locality: Saline River, near Benton railroad bridge, at Benton, Saline County, Arkansas, U.S.A.

North America: Mississippi River basin from northern Illinois to Louisiana, and from eastern Kentucky to central Kansas and Oklahoma in the USA; Gulf Slope drainages from Mobile Bay in Alabama to Guadalupe River in Texas, USA.
Inhabits sand-gravel riffles and runs near debris and among tree roots along undercut banks in creeks to large rivers.

The madtoms are well suited to aquarium life. Provide river gravel and smooth rounded stones for hiding places during the day. A power filter at one end of the tank will provide the conditions of a flowing stream for these catfish. As with most of this genus, handle with care: the pectoral fin spine has a poison gland at its base.

Feeds on aquatic insect immatures dominated by mayflies, caddisflies, midges, and blackflies. In the aquarium they like most meaty food, such as cut-up earth worms, frozen bloodworm and prawns. They will also take tablet and pellet foods. A varied diet will keep them in optimum health.
Can be housed with other North American fishes such as minnows, darters and shiners.
Etymology: from the Greek notos, meaning back, and oura, meaning tail, in reference to the confluent adipose and caudal fins. The specific epithet refers to its black (nocturnus = night) colour.

Description: This species is moderately robust. The head is depressed, rounded above with the upper jaw overhanging the lower. 4 pairs of barbels. Pectoral fin spine with anterior edge smooth, posterior edge roughened or with 3–5 serrations. Anal fin is short, 15–20 rays. Colouration: Body has a uniform colour of a brown back with the sides lighter with dark freckles. The belly is yellowish. The bases of the median fins are dusky and lighter towards the edges, margins are clear.

Etymology: nocturnus means nocturnal, referring to the dark colouration.

IUCN Red List: Least Concern in view of the large extent of occurrence, large number of subpopulations, large population size, and lack of major threats.
